references.text: This text in Leviticus gives a detailed list of unclean birds that are not to be eaten, which parallels the legislation in Deuteronomy regarding clean and unclean birds.
Here it mentions which flying insects are permitted to eat, adding to the understanding of what is considered clean food with wings.
The preceding context in the same chapter lists unclean birds, and verse 20 summarizes that all other clean birds are allowed to be eaten.
Peter's vision concerning clean and unclean animals, including birds, shows the New Testament understanding of how the food laws in the Old Testament were fulfilled in Christ.
